# Pawel Lewtak and Emmy Sharp + 2 others
Date: 2026-11-02 | Duration: 16.75m

## Summary
A backend developer with an AI focus discussed using GrowthBook on a real-estate website platform involving microservices, legacy systems, PHP, JavaScript, and Node. GrowthBook supports A/B tests, feature flags, and hiding unreleased features from target audiences because staging was insufficient for internal production demonstrations. Registration and Chrome extension setup were smooth: the existing login was recognized, flags appeared immediately, and enabled or disabled flags were easy to manage. However, overrides were unstable: after refreshes, version A repeatedly appeared instead of version B, even though the Boolean remained true, and subpage behavior was inconsistent. Repeated toggles and browser-cache clearing produced mixed results. Possible contributing factors included Cloudflare, AWS, or the legacy codebase, but the root cause remained unclear. A previous custom tool offered server-side computation, IP-location targeting, browser-header targeting, Poland-only targeting, and 10% audience testing. GrowthBook remained appealing for future or personal projects, especially with a free, ongoing tier, while two-week trials felt too short. Support offered to investigate the extension issue, potentially using screenshots.

## Keywords
Feature flagging, Chrome extension, A/B testing, Onboarding experience, Caching issues, Free tier
